examples.knowledge_point: Calculating Indefinite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
examples.worked_solution:
Let $u = x^2+1.$ Then, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{3}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{2}\cdot x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {x}^{2}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}\,\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \overset{u-1}{\overset{⏞}{{x}^{2}}}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}\cdot \overset{\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u}{\overset{⏞}{x\,\text{d}x}} \\  & =\int (u-1)\sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int (u-1){u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int ({u}^{3/2}-{u}^{1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{2}{5}{u}^{5/2}-\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{5}({x}^{2}+1)^{5/2}-\frac{1}{3}({x}^{2}+1)^{3/2}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\sqrt{({x}^{2}+1)^{5}}-\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{({x}^{2}+1)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$
